<p>‘Where is this place?’</p><p>The very next day after hearing about it from Se-rin, I got into the car the Association had prepared and headed there. The gate’s location must have been classified, because the moment I got in the car, I had to put on a blindfold and earplugs. After about three hours of driving, we finally arrived somewhere in the mountains.</p><p>Since the Association President had given the order directly, I had no choice but to comply. I instinctively felt uneasy—after all, nothing ever went smoothly when the Association was involved. But Se-rin must have noticed my anxiety, because she reassured me that except for a tiny minority, most Hunters who entered the gate came back out in less than half a day, and even that minority all returned within a day. So it would be fine.</p><p>A temporary base had already been set up in front of the gate, bustling with Hunters and Association staff.</p><p>That was when a familiar-faced man stepped out of one of the tents.</p><p>‘Han Ji-hyeok…’</p><p>As soon as Han Ji-hyeok emerged from the tent, all ten of us A-rank Hunters—myself included—instinctively turned our gazes toward him.</p><p>“Thanks for coming, everyone. I know you’re all busy. You’ve already heard the mission details, so I’ll keep it brief. You’ll be entering the gate with me. Don’t worry—nothing worth worrying about will happen.”</p><p>After that, Han Ji-hyeok gave a quick recap of the mission. Hearing that he’d be going in with us did little to ease my unease, but seeing him in a suit rather than combat gear made it seem like we weren’t actually going in to fight.</p><p>Once Han Ji-hyeok finished speaking, an Association staff member gave us a few simple precautions.</p><p>First, after following the guide to the destination, upon meeting CODE: ECHO, we were to immediately kneel on one knee and not lift our heads until CODE: ECHO addressed us by name.</p><p>Second, we were to use formal speech when speaking to CODE: ECHO.</p><p>Third, if we needed to call for CODE: ECHO, we were to use the title “Your Majesty.”</p><p>They added that as long as we followed these three rules, nothing would happen to us. Then, we followed Han Ji-hyeok into the gate.</p><p>It seemed the Association referred to the boss of this gate as “Echo.”</p><p>“S-Seong-hyeon, shall we go in?”</p><p>“Yeah…”</p><p>I turned to look at Se-rin, and she seemed pretty nervous too.</p><p>“Se-rin, are you scared?”</p><p>Se-rin hesitated at my question before sighing and answering,</p><p>“Yes, actually. Even when I told you about it yesterday, it felt so unreal that I couldn’t really wrap my head around it. But now that we’re actually here… it’s a little scary.”</p><p>“Want me to hold your hand while we go in?”</p><p>I held out my hand, putting on a playful expression to lighten the mood, but Se-rin’s reaction wasn’t what I expected.</p><p>“Y-Yes…”</p><p>“Hm?”</p><p>Se-rin’s face flushed red, then she smiled and grabbed my hand.</p><p>“…”</p><p>In the end, I walked into the gate with Se-rin, our hands tightly clasped.</p><p>***</p><p>“W-What the…”</p><p>“It’s real…”</p><p>“J-Jeez…”</p><p>As soon as we stepped through the gate, just as Se-rin had said, a blond man in a perfectly tailored suit stood before us.</p><p>On the man’s shoulders sat what looked like goat heads—whether they were part of his body or attached, I couldn’t tell. He wore an old-fashioned suit reminiscent of the Renaissance.</p><p>The Hunters finally seemed to grasp the reality of the situation, each muttering to themselves. But the real shock came after that.</p><p>“Association President Han Ji-hyeok, welcome. My master has been awaiting you.”</p><p>The blond man bowed to Han Ji-hyeok, who returned the gesture with a nod of his own.</p><p>Watching a monster communicate with a human as if it were perfectly normal, Se-rin and I—along with the other Hunters—stood frozen, unable to process the unbelievable sight before us.</p><p>“Alright, everyone, snap out of it. Let’s move.”</p><p>At Han Ji-hyeok’s words, we barely managed to collect ourselves and followed him and the blond man.</p><p>‘Don’t forget the mission.’</p><p>This mission wasn’t just about meeting the leader—it was about exchanging as many words as possible to gather information.</p><p>The Association had sent many Hunters here before, yet they’d barely obtained any useful intel. Where these beings came from, why they were here… whether there were more like them capable of communication, why they were interested in humans—everything was shrouded in mystery.</p><p>We walked in silence toward the black castle. Not a single monster was in sight. The massive fortress standing alone on the obsidian earth exuded an eerie yet ancient grandeur.</p><p>At some point, Se-rin had taken my hand again, gripping it tightly as we walked.</p><p>Once inside the castle, we were too busy taking in the interior to focus on anything else. Shockingly, it looked almost identical to a human-made castle—something straight out of a fantasy novel.</p><p>After climbing stairs and walking down hallways, we finally arrived in front of a massive door.</p><p>The blond man glanced at Han Ji-hyeok, gave a nod, then stepped forward and announced,</p><p>“My lord, the guests have arrived.”</p><p>Instinctively, my body began to tremble. My senses screamed that an overwhelming presence awaited beyond that door.</p><p>“Enter.”</p><p>A bewitching female voice echoed from beyond the door, and as the blond man placed his hand on it, the door began to creak open slowly.</p><p>Before we entered, the Association member had only given us a briefing that lasted about five minutes. At the time, I’d wondered if they were being too careless, but as the door opened, we instinctively bowed our heads and fixed our gazes on the floor.</p><p>It was an instinctive terror—we had no idea what might happen if we met the eyes of whatever lay beyond.</p><p>The only one among us who didn’t lower his head was Han Ji-hyeok.</p><p>Once the door was fully open, we followed the blond man, eyes still downcast, along a path lined with purple silk.</p><p>Han Ji-hyeok, seemingly familiar with the place from his many visits, strode confidently down a different path and took a seat in a prepared chair.</p><p>The blond man stopped walking and addressed us.</p><p>“All of you, pay your respects.”</p><p>We dropped to one knee in unison.</p><p>“···.”</p><p>In front of us was a set of stairs, and atop them stood the one called *Echo*—the leader of this Gate—watching us. Yet for a long while, she said nothing, and a heavy silence stretched on for several minutes.</p><p>Then, after a few more minutes, she finally let out a deep, almost bored sigh before speaking.</p><p>“Only you remain. The rest of these vermin may leave.”</p><p>‘*You*?’</p><p>I couldn’t lift my head to see who she was referring to, but I was sure we were all thinking the same thing.</p><p>‘*Please, let me be one of the ‘rest of these vermin’…*’</p><p>The blond man walked in front of us. The *clack* of his shoes against the floor felt like it was squeezing my heart.</p><p>And when he stopped right in front of me, it felt like the world was collapsing.</p><p>“Ah, that one’s name is Yoon Seong-hyeon, Your Majesty. Send everyone out except for Seong-hyeon…”</p><p>At Han Ji-hyeok’s words, I realized with a sinking feeling that I was the unlucky winner.</p><p>‘*Fuck.*’</p><p>*Squeeeeak—THUD!*</p><p>The other nine… no, the other nine *Hunters* immediately stood, bowed, and exited the room. The door shut behind them.</p><p>“Lift your head.”</p><p>I couldn’t bring myself to do it. Fear wasn’t the issue—my brain had simply short-circuited, unable to process what was happening. All I could do was stare at the floor, cold sweat dripping down my face.</p><p>“Seong-hyeon-gong, please raise your head.”</p><p>“···.”</p><p>It was only when the blond man whispered beside me that my mind snapped back to reality. I slowly lifted my head and met the gaze of the figure seated on the stairs above me.</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291021" loading="lazy">
</p><p>That figure had long, flowing white hair, crimson eyes… and, incredibly, horns protruding from its head. It sat upon a throne, looking down at me.</p><p>When our eyes met, a chill ran through my entire body.</p><p>“Come closer.”</p><p>At its command, I stood up and climbed the stairs toward it.</p><p>As I held its gaze, a flood of thoughts suddenly surged into my mind.</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291022" loading="lazy">
</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291023" loading="lazy">
</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291024" loading="lazy">
</p><p>It felt as though the being was forcibly extracting memories from my mind. One after another, images of Yu-na, Na-hyeon, and Ji-hyeon flashed through my thoughts.</p><p>“W-what…?”</p><p>My legs gave out, and I staggered. The blond man was suddenly at my side, steadying me by the shoulder. “Are you alright, Seong-hyeon? His Majesty merely skimmed through your memories. There’s no need to be alarmed.”</p><p>Once my head cleared, the being stared at me for a few seconds before reacting in a way I never expected.</p><p>“Ha!”</p><p>A burst of laughter.</p><p>The being threw its head back and laughed like a madman. The room echoed with its laughter for over a minute. When I turned my head slightly, I saw Han Ji-hyeok staring at me, equally bewildered.</p><p>Finally, the being stopped laughing, clutching its stomach, and spoke.</p><p>“You are the most amusing human I have ever encountered. Han Ji-hyeok, you may leave us for a moment.”</p><p>“…Yes, Your Majesty.”</p><p>Even Han Ji-hyeok, my last psychological line of defense, left the room. Now, only I, the blond man, and the being remained.</p><p>After Han Ji-hyeok exited, the being addressed me.</p><p>“I am surprised. I did not know that humans other than my kin practiced incest.”</p><p>“W-what? N-no… Your Majesty?”</p><p>The words slipped out before I could stop them. I barely managed to tack on the honorific “Your Majesty” at the end.</p><p>“I am aware that lesser races avoid incest. Do not worry—I will not speak of this to your kind. I do not make idle threats.”</p><p>I wasn’t sure what he meant, but judging by the blond man’s words about scanning my memories… it seemed like he’d seen my family’s secret in them.</p><p>“Y-yes, Your Majesty…”</p><p>“How fascinating… You’re more interesting than every other human I’ve ever seen. Where did you get that armband?”</p><p>“I-I found it. Your Majesty.”</p><p>I’d blurted that out on instinct, but even this answer seemed to amuse him—he burst into laughter again.</p><p>“For one of my old friend’s belongings… to be worn by the most interesting human of all. How intriguing.”</p><p>I racked my brain for what to say, but no clever response came to mind.</p><p>“S-should I return it… Your Majesty?”</p><p>He laughed even harder at my answer.</p><p>‘What the hell? Am I about to die here?’</p><p>After staring at me for a few more minutes, he spoke again.</p><p>“Where’s the other one? You’re only wearing one. And you don’t need to call me ‘Your Majesty’—just answer comfortably.”</p><p>The blond man flinched, as if omitting the title was some incredible privilege, and stared at me.</p><p>“There’s another one?”</p><p>“Hmm… I see… Well, never mind. Nerus!”</p><p>“Yes, Your Majesty.”</p><p>The blond man knelt on one knee and bowed his head to the being.</p><p>‘So this man’s name is Nerus…’</p><p>“It’s decided! I shall live among humans with this one.”</p><p>“Yes, Your Majesty. I shall prepare at once.”</p><p>I had no idea what these two were talking about. If I was going to die, I at least had to say something first.</p><p>“What do you mean by ‘live together’?”</p><p>“I’ve taken an interest in the human world and was looking for someone to guide me there. You seem like you’d be entertaining to have around…”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>“Yes, I’ll take you as my guide. Consider it a great honor.”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>“Nerus, we leave at once.”</p><p>“Yes, Your Majesty.”</p><p>I was well and truly fucked.</p>
